zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
Meccan
﷽
﴿طسم﴾: what was mentioned about this has already preceded. ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 2]: one says "بانَ الشَّيْءُ" and "أبانَ" with a single meaning (the thing became clear); and one says "بانَ الشَّيْءُ" and "أبَنْتُهُ أنا" (I made it clear). [Translator's note: the source vocalises the first instance as بِانَ.] So the meaning of "مُبِينٌ" is: making clear its news and its blessing, making clear truth from falsehood and the lawful from the unlawful, making clear that the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ is true, because no one is able to produce its like, and making clear the stories of the prophets.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿نَتْلُو عَلَيْكَ مِن نَبَإ مُوسى وفِرْعَوْنَ بِالحَقِّ﴾, i.e. of the news of Moses and the news of Pharaoh. His saying: ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ means: "who believe it to be true (يُصَدِّقُونَ)".

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلا في الأرْضِ﴾ means: "he transgressed (طَغى)". ﴿وَجَعَلَ أهْلَها شِيَعًا﴾: the meaning of "شِيَعٌ" is: factions, i.e. he made every faction such that its members back one another up in what they do.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَسْتَضْعِفُ طائِفَةً مِنهم يُذَبِّحُ أبْناءَهم ويَسْتَحْيِي نِساءَهُمْ﴾: the meaning of "نِساءَهم" here is that he used to let their daughters live. He did that only because one of the soothsayers told him: "A child will be born at that time who will be the cause of the end of your kingdom." So how astonishing is Pharaoh's foolishness: if the soothsayer was truthful in his view, then what use was the killing; and if he was lying, then what sense was there in the killing?

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَنُرِيدُ أنْ نَمُنَّ عَلى الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا في الأرْضِ﴾ means the Children of Israel, whom Pharaoh held weak. ﴿وَنَجْعَلَهم أئِمَّةً﴾, i.e. We make them rulers who are followed. ﴿وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ الوارِثِينَ﴾, i.e. they inherit Pharaoh and his kingdom.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهم في الأرْضِ ونُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾: the reading is the accusative, "نُمَكِّنَ" and "نُرِيَ"; the nominative is permissible: "وَنُمَكِّنُ لَهم في الأرْضِ ونُرِي", with a sukūn on the yāʾ. Whoever uses the accusative conjoins it to "نَمُنَّ", so the meaning is: "and that We establish and that We show (وَأنْ نُمَكِّنَ وأنْ نُرِيَ)". Whoever uses the nominative does so with the meaning "and We establish (وَنَحْنُ نُمَكِّنُ)". It has also been read: "وَيُرى فِرْعَوْنُ وهامانُ وجُنُودُهُما"; then "يُرى" is in the position of an accusative, by conjunction with "نُمَكِّنَ", and it may be in the position of a nominative, as "and Pharaoh and Hāmān and their armies will see (وَسَيُرى فِرْعَوْنُ وهامانُ وجُنُودُهُما)". [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the attested reading is وَيَرى.]

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَأوْحَيْنا إلى أُمِّ مُوسى أنْ أرْضِعِيهِ﴾: it was said that the revelation (al-waḥy) here is what Allah cast into her heart. What follows this indicates — and Allah knows best — that it was a revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by way of informing, as a guarantee to her: ﴿إنّا رادُّوهُ إلَيْكِ وجاعِلُوهُ مِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾; and it is indicated by: ﴿وَلِتَعْلَمَ أنَّ وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 13]. It has been said that al-waḥy here is inspiration (al-ilhām), and it is possible that Allah cast into her heart that he would be returned to her and that he would be a messenger; but informing is clearer here, I mean that al-waḥy here is informing. The root sense of al-waḥy in the whole language is: informing in secret; that is why inspiration came to be called waḥy.
And His saying: ﴿فَألْقِيهِ في اليَمِّ﴾: "al-yamm (اليَمُّ)" is the sea.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فالتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا وحَزَنًا﴾, and "وَحُزْنًا" is permissible. The meaning of "لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا" is: so that the matter would end up thus — not that they sought him and took him for this — just as you say of someone who earned wealth and that led to his ruin: "So-and-so only earned for his death (إنَّما كَسَبَ فُلانٌ لِحَتْفِهِ)", while he did not seek the wealth for death. Similar to it is: "So for death is what the mother bears (فَلِلْمَوْتِ ما تَلِدُ الوالِدَةُ)", i.e. she did not bear him seeking that her child die, but the outcome is that.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقالَتِ امْرَأتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِي ولَكَ﴾: "قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ" is nominative by implying "he is a comfort of the eye for me and for you (هو قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ لِي ولَكَ)", and this is a complete pause (waqf al-tamām). It is ugly to put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) being "لا تَقْتُلُوهُ", for then it would be as if he had already known that he was a comfort of the eye for him. Putting it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ is permissible though far-fetched, with the meaning "since he is a comfort of the eye for me and for you, do not kill him (إذا كانَ قُرَّةَ عَيْنٍ لِي ولَكَ فَلا تَقْتُلْهُ)". The accusative is permissible but do not read it, because no transmission of a reading has come with it; the accusative would be with the meaning "Do not kill a comfort of the eye for me and for you — do not kill him (لا تَقْتُلُوا قُرَّةَ عَيْنٍ لِي ولَكَ لا تَقْتُلُوهُ)", just as you say: "Zayd — do not hit him (زَيْدًا لا تَضْرِبْهُ)".

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأصْبَحَ فُؤادُ أُمِّ مُوسى فارِغًا﴾: the meaning is: it became empty of everything except the remembrance of Moses; and it was said: except of anxiety over Moses; and the meaning is one. ﴿إنْ كادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ﴾: the meaning is: "she very nearly disclosed that he was her son (إنْ كادَتْ لَتُظْهِرُ أنَّهُ ابْنُها)". It has been read "فَرِغًا", and most read "فارِغًا". ﴿لَوْلا أنْ رَبَطْنا عَلى قَلْبِها﴾ means: "had it not been for Our binding of her heart (لَوْلا رَبْطُنا عَلى قَلْبِها)"; and "binding of the heart (الرَّبْطُ عَلى القَلْبِ)" is inspiring patience, and strengthening and fortifying it.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَقالَتْ لأُخْتِهِ قُصِّيهِ﴾, in the sense of: "follow his trail (اِتْبَعِي أثَرَهُ)".
﴿فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ عَنْ جُنُبٍ﴾ means: "so she followed him and watched him from afar (فاتَّبَعَتْهُ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ عَنْ جُنُبٍ)", i.e. from a distance, watching without giving the impression that she saw him. One says: "بَصُرْتُ بِهِ عَنْ جُنُبٍ" and "عَنْ جَنابَةٍ" when you look at him from a distance. The poet said:
؎فَلا تَحْرِمَنِّي نائِلًا عَنْ جَنابَةٍ ∗∗∗ فَإنِّي امْرُؤٌ وسْطَ القِبابِ غَرِيبُ
(So do not deny me a gift on account of distance, for I am a man who is a stranger among the tents.)
I.e. do not deny me a gift from afar, even though I am far from you.

zajjaj:12-12.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَحَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِ المَراضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ means: "before We returned him to his mother". Moses did not take from a breast, i.e. he did not suckle from a breast, until he was returned to his mother and suckled from her; this is the meaning of ﴿وَحَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِ المَراضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾. ﴿فَقالَتْ هَلْ أدُلُّكم عَلى أهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُ لَكُمْ﴾, i.e. the sister of Moses, peace be upon him, said, when nursing him had proved impossible for them: ﴿هَلْ أدُلُّكم عَلى أهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُ لَكم وهم لَهُ ناصِحُونَ﴾. When they heard her saying "وَهم لَهُ ناصِحُونَ", they said: "You have recognised this boy's family, by your saying: 'and they will be sincere to him'." She said: "By 'they [are sincere] to him' I meant: they are sincere to the king." So she directed them to the mother of Moses, and he was handed to her to rear him for them, as they reckoned.

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying: ﴿فَرَدَدْناهُ إلى أُمِّهِ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُها ولا تَحْزَنَ ولِتَعْلَمَ أنَّ وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾ means what she had been promised in what was revealed to her, in His saying: ﴿إنّا رادُّوهُ إلَيْكِ وجاعِلُوهُ مِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 7]; and it became settled with her that he would be a prophet.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَمّا بَلَغَ أشُدَّهُ واسْتَوى﴾: it was said: "al-ashudd (الأشُدُّ)" is thirty-some years, which is between thirty-three and thirty-nine. The interpretation of "بَلَغَ أشُدَّهُ" is: he attained the full extent of a man's strength. It was said that the meaning of "واسْتَوى" is: he reached forty; and it is possible that "اِسْتَوى" means he truly attained the full reality of reaching maturity.
And His saying: ﴿آتَيْناهُ حُكْمًا وعِلْمًا﴾: so Moses, peace be upon him, had knowledge and judgement before he was sent. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾: so Allah made the granting of knowledge and wisdom a recompense for good-doing, because they both lead to Paradise, which is the recompense of the good-doers. The wise scholar is one who puts his knowledge to use, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَبِئْسَ ما شَرَوْا بِهِ أنْفُسَهم لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 102], and so, since they did not act on knowledge, He made them ignorant.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَدَخَلَ المَدِينَةَ عَلى حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِن أهْلِها﴾: it has come in the exegesis that he entered it at the time of the midday rest (al-qāʾila), which is the middle of the day.
And His saying: ﴿هَذا مِن شِيعَتِهِ وهَذا مِن عَدُوِّهِ﴾: this is a place with a subtlety in it, namely that "هَذا" (this) is said of someone absent. The meaning is: "he found in it two men, one of them of his party and one of them of his enemy", and "هَذا" and "هَذا" were said of them by way of narrating presence (ḥikāya li-l-ḥaḍra), i.e. "he found in it two men such that, when an onlooker looked at them, he would say: this one is of his party and this one is of his enemy". ﴿فاسْتَغاثَهُ الَّذِي مِن شِيعَتِهِ﴾, i.e. he asked him for help. The one of his party was of the Children of Israel, and the one of his enemy was of Pharaoh's people. It has come in the exegesis that Pharaoh was a man from the people of Iṣṭakhr; and it is said that the man who was of his enemy was a man of the Copts, and it was also said: of the people of Iṣṭakhr.
﴿فَوَكَزَهُ مُوسى فَقَضى عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. he killed him. "al-wakz (الوَكْزُ)" is to strike with your clenched fist; and it has been said: he struck him with the staff.
And His saying: ﴿قالَ هَذا مِن عَمَلِ الشَّيْطانِ﴾ indicates that his killing him was by mistake, and that Moses had not been commanded to kill or to fight. ﴿قالَ رَبِّ إنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فاغْفِرْ لِي فَغَفَرَ لَهُ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 16]

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأصْبَحَ في المَدِينَةِ خائِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإذا الَّذِي اسْتَنْصَرَهُ بِالأمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُ﴾, i.e. he cries to him for help; "al-istiṣrākh (الاِسْتِصْراخُ)" is crying for rescue and asking for help. ﴿قالَ لَهُ مُوسى إنَّكَ لَغَوِيٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾

zajjaj:19-19.t: And His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا أنْ أرادَ أنْ يَبْطِشَ بِالَّذِي هو عَدُوٌّ لَهُما﴾, and it is also read "يَبْطُشُ". The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "When the one crying for help wanted Moses to seize the one who was an enemy to them both, and Moses did not do it, Moses said: you are clearly a misguided man." ﴿قالَ يا مُوسى أتُرِيدُ أنْ تَقْتُلَنِي كَما قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا بِالأمْسِ إنْ تُرِيدُ إلا أنْ تَكُونَ جَبّارًا في الأرْضِ وما تُرِيدُ أنْ تَكُونَ مِنَ المُصْلِحِينَ﴾: so he divulged [the matter] against Moses, peace be upon him. It is said that whoever kills two people is a tyrant (jabbār). "al-jabbār (الجَبّارُ)" in the language is the haughty one who does not humble himself to the command of Allah; so the killer of a believer is a jabbār, and every killer is a jabbār, whether he kills one person or a group, wrongfully.

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ رَجُلٌ مِن أقْصى المَدِينَةِ يَسْعى﴾: it is said that he was the believer of Pharaoh's family, and that he was a carpenter. The meaning of "يَسْعى" is: he runs. ﴿قالَ يا مُوسى إنَّ المَلأ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ﴾: "al-malaʾ (المَلَأُ)" are the nobles of the people, those who are looked up to; and the meaning of "يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ" is: they are urging one another to kill you. ﴿فاخْرُجْ إنِّي لَكَ مِنَ النّاصِحِينَ﴾, i.e. leave the city. His saying "لَكَ" is not part of the ṣila (relative clause) of "النّاصِحِينَ", because the ṣila is not placed before the relative. The sense in His saying "إنِّي لَكَ" is that it is explanatory, as if he said: "I am of the sincere advisers, who advise you sincerely (إنِّي مِنَ النّاصِحِينَ يَنْصَحُونَ لَكَ)". The usage is "نَصَحْتُ لَكَ", and it is more common than "نَصَحْتُكَ".

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَخَرَجَ مِنها خائِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ﴾, i.e. watching out lest someone catch up with him to kill him, and looking at the tracks.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِي مِنَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ means: "from Pharaoh's people".

zajjaj:22-22.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقاءَ مَدْيَنَ قالَ عَسى رَبِّي أنْ يَهْدِيَنِي سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾: "Madyan (مَدْيَنُ)" was a watering place belonging to the people of Shuʿayb. It is said that between it and Egypt is a journey of eight days, as between Basra and Kufa. Moses, peace be upon him, had left Egypt. The meaning of ﴿تِلْقاءَ مَدْيَنَ﴾ is: he took the road on which the direction of Madyan lay. ﴿قالَ عَسى رَبِّي أنْ يَهْدِيَنِي سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾: "al-sabīl (السَّبِيلُ)" is the road, and "سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ" is the straight middle of the road in its evenness.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا ورَدَ ماءَ مَدْيَنَ﴾: "مَدْيَنَ" is in the position of a genitive (khafḍ), but it is a diptote (lā yanṣarif), because it is the name of a place. ﴿وَلَمّا ورَدَ ماءَ مَدْيَنَ وجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِنَ النّاسِ يَسْقُونَ﴾: "أُمَّةً" is: a group. ﴿وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ امْرَأتَيْنِ تَذُودانِ﴾, i.e. they were holding back their sheep from coming near the place of the water, because whoever was stronger than them at watering would drive them away from the water. ﴿قالَ ما خَطْبُكُما﴾, i.e. "what is your matter? (ما أمْرُكُما؟)"; its meaning is: "what are you after? (ما تَخْطُبانِ؟)", i.e. "what do you intend by holding your sheep back from the water?" "قالَتا لا نَسْقِي حَتّى يَصْدُرَ الرِّعاءُ" — and it has been read: ﴿حَتّى يُصْدِرَ الرِّعاءُ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the dāl, i.e. we are not able to water until the shepherds take their sheep back, having drunk, and the place becomes empty, and we water. Whoever reads "يَصْدُرَ" with ḍamma on the dāl, its meaning is: until the shepherds go back. "al-riʿāʾ (الرِّعاءُ)" is the plural of "rāʿin (راعٍ)" (shepherd), as one says "ṣāḥib (صاحِبٌ)" and "ṣiḥāb (صِحابٌ)".
And His saying: ﴿وَأبُونا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾: the point of His saying ﴿وَأبُونا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ is: he cannot come to the water and water [the flock]; that is why we, though we are women, have needed to do the watering.

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿فَسَقى لَهُما ثُمَّ تَوَلّى إلى الظِّلِّ﴾, the verse: i.e. he watered for them before the time at which they used to water. It is said that he lifted a stone off the well which only ten people could lift; and it was said that Moses at that time was in such poverty that he could not afford half a date.

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying: ﴿فَجاءَتْهُ إحْداهُما﴾: the meaning is: "When their sheep had drunk, they returned to their father and told him the story of Moses and his watering their sheep, and they had come to him before their usual time with their sheep already watered; so he sent one of them to call Moses, and she came to him walking shyly." It has come in the exegesis that she was not a woman who went out and came in much, i.e. she walked as one who is not accustomed to going in and out, modest and bashful. ﴿قالَتْ إنَّ أبِي يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أجْرَ ما سَقَيْتَ لَنا﴾: the meaning is: so he answered her and went with her to her father. ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهُ وقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ القَصَصَ﴾, i.e. he told him his story about his killing the man, and that they were seeking him to kill him. ﴿قالَ لا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾: that was because the people were not within Pharaoh's kingdom, so Shuʿayb informed Moses that he had escaped from fear and that [Pharaoh] had no power over him — I mean by "the people" the people of Madyan among whom the father of the two women lived. It is said in the exegesis that he was the nephew of Shuʿayb the Prophet, peace be upon him.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
﴿قالَتْ إحْداهُما يا أبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ﴾, i.e. take him as a hired man.
﴿إنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ القَوِيُّ الأمِينُ﴾, i.e. the best one you can employ is one who is strong enough for your work and fulfils the trust in it. She said "القَوِيُّ الأمِينُ" — she described him with strength because he watered her sheep with strength and vigour; and it was said: because of his strength in lifting the stone which fewer than ten people could not lift; and it has been said that fewer than forty people could not lift it. As for her describing him with trustworthiness, it was said that when Moses went with her to her father, he went ahead of her and told her to stay behind him and direct him along the way; he feared that if she were in front of him the wind would catch her wrap and the shape of her body would show. That is what she recognised of his trustworthiness.

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَ إنِّي أُرِيدُ أنْ أُنْكِحَكَ إحْدى ابْنَتَيَّ هاتَيْنِ﴾: the meaning of "أُنْكِحَكَ" is: I marry you [to]. ﴿عَلى أنْ تَأْجُرَنِي ثَمانِيَ حِجَجٍ﴾, i.e. that you be a hired man for me for eight years. ﴿فَإنْ أتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِن عِنْدِكَ﴾, i.e. that is by your generosity, not obligatory upon you.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿قالَ ذَلِكَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ﴾, i.e. "that which you have described to me is between me and you"; its meaning is: "what you have stipulated against me is yours, and what you have stipulated for me is mine; thus is the matter between us." Then he said: ﴿أيَّما الأجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلا عُدْوانَ عَلَيَّ﴾. "al-ʿudwān (العُدْوانُ)" is going beyond bounds in wrongdoing. "عُدْوانَ" is accusative through "لا" [the lā of generic negation]. Had it been read "فَلا عُدْوانٌ عَلَيَّ", it would be permissible from two angles. One of them is that "لا" puts [its noun] in the nominative, like "لَيْسَ", as the poet said:
؎مَن صَدَّ عَنْ نِيرانِها ∗∗∗ فَأنا ابْنُ قَيْسٍ لا بَراحُ
(Whoever turns away from its fires — I am Ibn Qays: there is no leaving.)
And it is possible that "عُدْوانٌ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with "عَلَيَّ" the khabar (predicate), and "لا" a negative that does not govern, as you say: "لا زَيْدٌ أخُوكَ، ولا عَمْرٌو" (neither Zayd is your brother, nor ʿAmr). "أيَّ" is in the position of the conditional (al-jazāʾ), accusative by "قَضَيْتُ", and the apodosis (jawāb al-jazāʾ) is "فَلا عُدْوانَ"; "ما" is redundant (zāʾida), emphatic; and the meaning is: "whichever of the two terms I complete, there is no transgression against me (أيَّ الأجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلا عُدْوانَ عَلَيَّ)".
And His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ عَلى ما نَقُولُ وكِيلٌ﴾, i.e. "and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is our witness over what we have contracted with one another".

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا قَضى مُوسى الأجَلَ وسارَ بِأهْلِهِ﴾: it is narrated that he completed the fuller of the two terms, which is ten years.
And His saying: ﴿آنَسَ مِن جانِبِ الطُّورِ نارًا﴾: "آنَسَ" means: he knew and saw. One says: "قَدْ آنَسْتُ ذَلِكَ الشَّخْصَ", i.e. I saw him. ﴿قالَ لأهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا إنِّي آنَسْتُ نارًا لَعَلِّي آتِيكم مِنها بِخَبَرٍ﴾, i.e. perhaps I will learn why it was lit, "أوْ جِذْوَةٍ مِنَ النّارِ": "al-jidhwa (الجِذْوَةُ)" is a thick piece of firewood. It is also read "أوْ جُذْوَةٍ" with ḍamma, and one says "جَذْوَةٌ" with fatḥa; there are three dialectal forms in it.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
And His saying: ﴿فِي البُقْعَةِ المُبارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾: it was called "blessed (مُبارَكَةً)" because Allah spoke to Moses there and sent him as a prophet. One says "بُقْعَةٌ" and "بَقْعَةٌ", with ḍamma and fatḥa, and both have been read. Whoever uses the plural "بِقاعًا", it is the plural of "بَقْعَةٌ" with fatḥa, like "قَصْعَةٌ" and "قِصاعٌ". Whoever says "بُقْعَةٌ" with ḍamma, the best plural is "بُقَعٌ", like "غُرْفَةٌ" and "غُرَفٌ"; and "بِقاعٌ" may also be used for "بُقْعَةٌ", like "حُفْرَةٌ" and "حِفارٌ".
And His saying: ﴿أنْ يا مُوسى﴾: "أنْ" is in the position of an accusative; the meaning is: "he was called with: O Moses (نُودِيَ بِأنَّهُ يا مُوسى)". Likewise ﴿وَأنْ ألْقِ عَصاكَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 31] is conjoined to it.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿فَلَمّا رَآها تَهْتَزُّ كَأنَّها جانٌّ ولّى مُدْبِرًا ولَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾ means: he did not turn round.
And His saying: ﴿أقْبِلْ ولا تَخَفْ إنَّكَ مِنَ الآمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. you are safe from any harm reaching you from it, though it is a snake.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿اسْلُكْ يَدَكَ في جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِن غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾, i.e. without leprosy. ﴿واضْمُمْ إلَيْكَ جَناحَكَ مِنَ الرَّهْبِ﴾, and "الرُّهْبِ" — both — and their meaning is one, like "al-rushd (الرُّشْدُ)" and "al-rashad (الرَّشَدُ)". The meaning of "your wing (جَناحِكَ)" here is the upper arm; and it is said: the whole arm is a wing.
And His saying: ﴿فَذانِكَ بُرْهانانِ﴾: it is read with the nūn light and with it doubled: "فَذانِّكَ". It is as though "فَذانِّكَ" is the dual of "ذَلِكَ" and "ذانِكَ" the dual of "ذاكَ"; the doubling of the nūn in "ذانِكَ" was made a substitute for the lām in ذَلِكَ. "بُرْهانانِ" means: two clear signs.
﴿إلى فِرْعَوْنَ ومَلَئِهِ﴾, i.e. We have sent you to Pharaoh and his chiefs with these two signs.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي﴾, and "يُصَدِّقْنِي", in the nominative and the jussive; both have been read. Whoever reads "يُصَدِّقُنِي" with ḍamma on the qāf, it is an attribute of His saying "رِدْءًا". "al-radʾ (الرَّدْءُ)" is help; you say: "رَدَأْتُهُ، أرْدَؤُهُ، رَدْءًا" when you help him; and "al-ridʾ (الرِّدْءُ)" is the helper. Whoever puts "يُصَدِّقْنِي" in the jussive does so as the answer to the request: "send him, [and] he will confirm me (أرْسِلْهُ يُصَدِّقْنِي)". Whoever puts "يُصَدِّقُنِي" in the nominative, the meaning is: "a helper confirming me (رِدْءًا مُصَدِّقًا لِي)".

zajjaj:35-35.t:
And His saying: ﴿قالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأخِيكَ﴾, i.e. We will help you through your brother. The word "upper arm (al-ʿaḍud)" is by way of a figure, because the arm's support is its upper arm; so every helper is an ʿaḍud. You say: "قَدْ عاضَدَنِي فُلانٌ عَلى الأمْرِ", i.e. he assisted me.
And His saying: ﴿وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُما سُلْطانًا﴾, i.e. a luminous, clear proof. Oil was called "al-salīṭ (السَّلِيطُ)" only because light is sought by it; so "al-sulṭān (السُّلْطانُ)" is the clearest of proofs.
And His saying: ﴿فَلا يَصِلُونَ إلَيْكُما بِآياتِنا﴾, i.e. by Our authority and Our proof. So "بِآياتِنا" is connected to (min ṣilat) "يَصِلُونَ", as if He said: "they will not reach you two; you will be protected from them by Our signs (لا يَصِلُونَ إلَيْكُما، تَمْتَنِعانِ مِنهم بِآياتِنا)". It is possible that "بِآياتِنا" is attached to "We will give you two authority by Our signs (نَجْعَلُ لَكُما سُلْطانًا بِآياتِنا)", i.e. a proof that indicates prophethood by Our signs, namely by the staff, the hand and the rest of the signs that Moses ﷺ was given. It is also possible that "بِآياتِنا" explains His saying: ﴿أنْتُما ومَنِ اتَّبَعَكُما الغالِبُونَ﴾, i.e. "you will prevail by Our signs (تَغْلِبُونَ بِآياتِنا)".

zajjaj:36-36.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهم مُوسى بِآياتِنا بَيِّناتٍ﴾: they did not bring any proof by which to repel the signs that had appeared, except that they said: "It is magic." When the sorcerers were gathered, they made clear that the signs of Moses, peace be upon him, were not magic; so Moses prevailed by the signs of Allah and His proof, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأوْقِدْ لِي يا هامانُ عَلى الطِّينِ﴾, i.e. make baked bricks; and it is said that Pharaoh was the first to make baked bricks. ﴿فاجْعَلْ لِي صَرْحًا﴾: "al-ṣarḥ (الصَّرْحُ)" is any wide, lofty building.
And His saying: ﴿لَعَلِّي أطَّلِعُ إلى إلَهِ مُوسى﴾: Pharaoh thought it would be possible for him to reach toward the sky with his tower and see the sky and what is in it. ﴿وَإنِّي لأظُنُّهُ مِنَ الكاذِبِينَ﴾: "al-ẓann (الظَّنُّ)" in the language is a kind [of thought] that can be doubt and can be certainty. Pharaoh's saying "وَإنِّي لَأظُنُّهُ" is an admission that he was doubtful and had not become certain that Moses was a liar. In this there is a clarification that he disbelieved in Moses without certainty that he was not a prophet, while it had occurred to him that he was a prophet, because the signs which are [the proof of] prophethood are not unknown to anyone of sound nature.
And His saying in another place: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أنْـزَلَ هَؤُلاءِ إلا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ بَصائِرَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 102] is evidence that he had bound Pharaoh with the decisive proof.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ وجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾: "al-yamm (اليَمُّ)" is the sea; it is the one called "Īsāf (إيسافُ)", and it is the one in which Pharaoh and his armies were drowned, in the region of Egypt.

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْناهم أئِمَّةً يَدْعُونَ إلى النّارِ﴾, i.e. whoever follows them is in the Fire. ﴿وَيَوْمَ القِيامَةِ لا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾, i.e. they have no helper and no protector from the punishment of Allah.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ مِن بَعْدِ ما أهْلَكْنا القُرُونَ الأُولى﴾: the last of the destruction of generations by punishment in this world was that He made those who denied Moses, who transgressed on the Sabbath, into despised apes upon their denying Moses, peace be upon him.
And His saying: ﴿بَصائِرَ لِلنّاسِ﴾, i.e. making clear for people; the meaning is: "We gave Moses the Book as insights for people (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ بَصائِرَ لِلنّاسِ)", i.e. this is the state of Our giving him the Book: making clear — We make it clear for people. ﴿وَهُدًى ورَحْمَةً﴾ is conjoined to "بَصائِرَ". Had it been read in the nominative, with the meaning "so it is guidance and mercy (فَهو هُدًى ورَحْمَةٌ)", it would be permissible; but the accusative is better, and I know of no one who read the nominative, so do not read it.

zajjaj:44-44.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما كُنْتَ بِجانِبِ الغَرْبِيِّ﴾, i.e. "you were not on the western side of the mountain (وَما كُنْتَ بِجانِبِ الجَبَلِ الغَرْبِيِّ)".

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَما كُنْتَ ثاوِيًا في أهْلِ مَدْيَنَ﴾, i.e. "you were not residing among the people of Madyan".

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿وَما كُنْتَ بِجانِبِ الطُّورِ إذْ نادَيْنا﴾ means: "when We called Moses". ﴿وَلَكِنْ رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ﴾: the meaning is: "You did not witness the stories of the prophets, nor were they recited to you; but We revealed them to you and narrated them to you as a mercy from your Lord," ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا﴾, i.e. so that you may acquaint them with the stories of those destroyed by punishment and those who won the reward. Had it been read "ولَكِنْ رَحْمَةٌ", it would be permissible, with the meaning: "but doing that is a mercy from your Lord (ولَكِنْ فِعْلُ ذَلِكَ رَحْمَةٌ مِن رَبِّكَ)". The accusative is with the meaning: "We did that for the sake of mercy (فَعَلْنا ذَلِكَ لِلرَّحْمَةِ)", as you say: "I did that seeking good (فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ ابْتِغاءَ الخَيْرِ)", i.e. "I did it for the seeking of good"; so it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا أنْ تُصِيبَهم مُصِيبَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُوا رَبَّنا لَوْلا أرْسَلْتَ إلَيْنا رَسُولا فَنَتَّبِعَ آياتِكَ ونَكُونَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. were it not for that, there would have been no need to send messengers and to make the argument against them one after another.

zajjaj:48-48.t: And His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهُمُ الحَقُّ مِن عِنْدِنا﴾, i.e. when the decisive proof came to them, whose delay they might have used as an excuse. ﴿قالُوا لَوْلا أُوتِيَ مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيَ مُوسى﴾: the meaning is: "Why was Muhammad not given the like of what Moses was given — may Allah bless them both — in the matter of the staff, the snake, the parting of the sea and the rest of the signs that Moses brought?" Yet they had disbelieved in the signs of Moses, just as they disbelieved in the signs of Muhammad, peace be upon them both. "قالُوا ساحْرانِ تَظاهَرا", i.e. who assisted each other. It has come in the exegesis that they meant Moses and Aaron; and they said: they meant Moses and Jesus; and it was said: they meant Moses and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. It has also been read: ﴿سِحْرانِ تَظاهَرا﴾, meaning two books; so they said: the Gospel and the Qur'an. And the evidence of whoever read ﴿سِحْرانِ﴾ [is in what follows]. [Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source and continues in the next entry; the source vocalises ساحْرانِ with a sukūn.]

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِكِتابٍ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ هو أهْدى مِنهُما﴾ — and this does not rule out "ساحِرانِ", because the meaning becomes: "Say: then bring a book from Allah that is better guidance than the two books of the two of them (قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِكِتابٍ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ هو أهْدى مِن كِتابَيْهِما)".

zajjaj:50-50.t: And His saying: ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكَ فاعْلَمْ أنَّما يَتَّبِعُونَ أهْواءَهُمْ﴾: then know that they have no proof for the disbelief they have embarked on; they have merely preferred whim in it, while they know that it [the message] is the truth.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ وصَّلْنا لَهُمُ القَوْلَ﴾, i.e. We set it out in detail, by setting out the mention of the prophets and their stories, and the stories of those who passed away, one joined to another. ﴿لَعَلَّهم يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾, i.e. so that they may take heed.

zajjaj:52-52.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِهِ هم بِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that these were a group of the People of the Book who used to hold to it, end at it and stop at its limits; they used to judge by the judgement of Allah, by the Book that was revealed before the Qur'an. When Muhammad ﷺ was sent and recited the Qur'an to them, they said: "We believe in it; it is the truth from our Lord." That was because the mention of Muhammad ﷺ was written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, so these did not oppose him obstinately; they believed and affirmed, and Allah praised them well.

zajjaj:54-54.t: And He said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أجْرَهم مَرَّتَيْنِ بِما صَبَرُوا﴾, i.e. they are given their reward for their belief in the Book that came before Muhammad ﷺ, and they are given their reward twice for belief in Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an. ﴿وَيَدْرَءُونَ بِالحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ﴾: the meaning of "وَيَدْرَؤُونَ" is: they repel, by the good deeds they know [to do], the bad deeds that preceded from them. ﴿وَمِمّا رَزَقْناهم يُنْفِقُونَ﴾, i.e. they give in charity.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿وَإذا سَمِعُوا اللَّغْوَ أعْرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾, i.e. when they hear what is not permissible and ought to be disregarded, they pay no attention to it. ﴿وَقالُوا لَنا أعْمالُنا ولَكم أعْمالُكم سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم لا نَبْتَغِي الجاهِلِينَ﴾: they do not mean by their saying here "سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم" the greeting; the meaning in it is: "they turned away from it and said: peace be upon you", i.e. between us and you is leaving each other alone and keeping clear (al-tasallum). This was before the Muslims were commanded to fight.

zajjaj:56-56.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّكَ لا تَهْدِي مَن أحْبَبْتَ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَن يَشاءُ﴾: the exegetes are agreed that it was revealed concerning Abū Ṭālib. It is possible that its revelation began concerning Abū Ṭālib while it is general, because none guides but Allah, and none directs aright or grants success but He; and likewise He leads astray whom He wills.

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿وَقالُوا إنْ نَتَّبِعِ الهُدى مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفْ مِن أرْضِنا﴾: they had said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We know that what you have brought is true, but we dislike, if we believe in you, being attacked and snatched away from our land." So Allah informed them that He had favoured them by making them secure in Mecca; He informed them that He had made them secure through the sanctity of the House and kept the enemy away from them, i.e. had they believed, it would be all the more fitting for [them to have] firm establishment, security and safety.

zajjaj:58-58.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِن قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَها﴾: "مَعِيشَتَها" is accusative by the dropping of "في" and the action of the verb (accusative by removal of the preposition); its interpretation is: "it exulted in its livelihood (بَطِرَتْ في مَعِيشَتِها)". "al-baṭar (البَطَرُ)" is transgressing through blessing.

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما كانَ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ القُرى حَتّى يَبْعَثَ في أُمِّها رَسُولا﴾: by "its mother (أُمِّها)" He means Mecca. He would not destroy it except for the wrongdoing of its people.

zajjaj:61-61.t: ﴿أفَمَن وعَدْناهُ وعْدًا حَسَنًا فَهو لاقِيهِ كَمَن مَتَّعْناهُ مَتاعَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ means the believer and the disbeliever. The believer is one who believed in Allah and His Messenger, obeyed Him and stopped at His command, so he is granted the recompense of that, which is Paradise. The one who was given the enjoyment of the life of this world is a disbeliever who did not believe in Allah, and then on the Day of Resurrection he is brought to the punishment; that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ هو يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ مِنَ المُحْضَرِينَ﴾. It has come in the exegesis that this verse was revealed concerning Muhammad ﷺ and Abū Jahl ibn Hishām: the Prophet ﷺ was promised a fair promise and he meets it in this world, in that he was given victory over his enemy in this world, and in the Hereafter he is in the highest ranks of Paradise; and Abū Jahl is among those brought [to punishment].

zajjaj:62-62.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُ أيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ﴾, i.e. the day He calls mankind. He called them "My partners (شُرَكائِي)" by way of narrating their own words; the meaning is: "Where are My partners according to your claim?" — and Allah is One, without partner.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ القَوْلُ﴾: the jinn and the devils. ﴿هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أغْوَيْنا أغْوَيْناهم كَما غَوَيْنا﴾: they mean mankind, i.e. we made error and misguidance seem attractive to them. ﴿أغْوَيْناهم كَما غَوَيْنا﴾, i.e. we led them astray as we went astray.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تَبَرَّأْنا إلَيْكَ﴾: they disowned one another and became enemies, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿الأخِلاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهم لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إلا المُتَّقِينَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]

zajjaj:64-64.t: And His saying: ﴿فَدَعَوْهم فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُمْ﴾, i.e. they did not answer them with any proof. ﴿وَرَأوُا العَذابَ لَوْ أنَّهم كانُوا يَهْتَدُونَ﴾: the answer of "لَوْ" is omitted — and Allah knows best —; the meaning: "had they been guided, they would not have followed them, nor seen the punishment".

zajjaj:68-68.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ ويَخْتارُ ما كانَ لَهُمُ الخِيَرَةُ﴾: the best pause is on "وَيَخْتارُ", with "ما" a negative; the meaning: "Your Lord creates what He wills, and your Lord chooses; they have no choice (لَيْسَ لَهُمُ الخِيرَةُ)", and "ما كانَتْ لَهُمُ الخِيَرَةُ", i.e. it is not for them to choose over Allah. This is one way. It is also possible that "ما" is in the sense of "الَّذِي" (relative noun), so the meaning would be: "and He chooses that in which there is the best choice for them (وَيَخْتارُ الَّذِي كانَ لَهم فِيهِ الخِيَرَةُ)", and the meaning of choosing here would be: what He makes them worship Him by, i.e. He chooses for them, in the worship of Him to which He calls them, that which holds the best for them. The first view is better, i.e. that "ما" be a negative.
And His saying: ﴿سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ وتَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: the meaning of "سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ" is declaring Him free of evil; so it is in the language, and so it has come from the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ اللَّيْلَ سَرْمَدًا إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾: "al-sarmad (السَّرْمَدُ)" in the language is the perpetual.
And His saying: ﴿مَن إلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكم بِضِياءٍ﴾, i.e. with daytime in which you can see, go about your livelihoods, and in which your fruits and plants are made good; because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the well-being of creation through night together with day, and if there were only one of them without the other, creation would perish. Likewise His saying concerning the day: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ النَّهارَ سَرْمَدًا إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 72]. He informed them that night and day are a mercy, and said: ﴿وَمِن رَحْمَتِهِ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ والنَّهارَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ ولِتَبْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 73]. The meaning is: "He made time for you as night and day, so that you may rest by night and seek of Allah's bounty by day." It is also possible [that it means] that you rest in both and seek of Allah's bounty in both; then the meaning is: "He made time for you as night and day, that you may rest in it and seek of His bounty."

zajjaj:75-75.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَنَـزَعْنا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا﴾, i.e. We drew out from every nation a prophet, i.e. We chose a prophet from it; and every prophet is a witness over his nation.
And His saying: ﴿فَقُلْنا هاتُوا بُرْهانَكُمْ﴾, i.e. bring a proof for what you believed, i.e. a demonstration that you were on the truth. ﴿فَعَلِمُوا أنَّ الحَقَّ لِلَّهِ﴾, i.e. they knew that the truth is the oneness of Allah and what His prophets brought.
And His saying: ﴿وَضَلَّ عَنْهم ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾, i.e. they did not benefit from anything they worshipped besides Allah; rather it harmed them with the greatest harm.

zajjaj:76-76.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إنَّ قارُونَ كانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسى﴾: "Qārūn (قارُونُ)" is a foreign name that is a diptote (lā yanṣarif); and even if it were of the pattern "fāʿūl" from Arabic, from "qarantu al-shayʾ (قَرَنْتُ الشَّيْءَ)" (I joined the thing), it would not be declined [as a triptote]; that is why it does not take tanwīn. [Translator's note: so in the source; a genuinely Arabic fāʿūl noun would normally be fully declinable.] It has come in the exegesis that Qārūn was the cousin of Moses and was one of the scholars of the Torah; he wronged Moses and set out to make trouble for him and to give him the lie. Part of his seeking to make trouble for him was that there was a notorious prostitute among the Children of Israel. Qārūn — who was the wealthiest person of his time — sent to her, ordering her to come to him while he was in a gathering of his companions, to tell lies about Moses and say: "He solicited me for indecency and suspicious conduct." Qārūn guaranteed her, if she did that, that he would admit her among his wives and give her a large gift for it. The woman came while Qārūn was sitting with his companions, and Allah granted her repentance. She said to herself: "I will have no occasion for repentance like this one." So she turned to the people of the gathering, with Qārūn present, and said to them: "This Qārūn sent to me, ordering me and asking me to tell lies about Moses and to say that he wanted me for indecency; and Qārūn is lying in that." When Qārūn heard her words he was confounded and struck speechless. The news reached Moses, peace be upon him, and Allah placed the matter of Qārūn in the hands of Moses and commanded the earth to obey him concerning him. Moses came upon Qārūn, and Qārūn sensed the calamity and said: "O Moses, have mercy on me." He said: "O earth, take him (يا أرْضُ خُذِيهِ)." So he and his house were swallowed up to his knees. He said: "O Moses, have mercy on me." He said: "O earth, take him," and he was swallowed up to his navel. Then he said: "O earth, take him," and he was swallowed up to his neck; and he begged Moses for mercy, and he said: "O earth, take him," and he was swallowed up until the earth sank down with him and his house. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَخَسَفْنا بِهِ وبِدارِهِ الأرْضَ فَما كانَ لَهُ مِن فِئَةٍ يَنْصُرُونَهُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وما كانَ مِنَ المُنْتَصِرِينَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 81]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ مِنَ الكُنُوزِ ما إنَّ مَفاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوءُ بِالعُصْبَةِ أُولِي القُوَّةِ﴾: it is narrated in the exegesis that his keys were made of hides, each the size of a finger, and they were carried on seventy mules, or sixty mules. It has also come that "مَفاتِحَهُ" means "his treasuries (خَزائِنَهُ)". It was said that the band (al-ʿuṣba) here is seventy men; and it was said: forty; and it was said: between fifteen and forty; and it was said: between three and ten. "al-ʿuṣba (العُصْبَةُ)" in the language is the group whose affair is one, who follow one another in action and are partisan for one another. The more likely of what has come in the exegesis is that "مَفاتِحَهُ" are "his treasuries", and that they are treasuries of wealth carried on seventy or on forty mules — and Allah knows best — because keys of hide, the size of a finger, carried on seventy mules for the treasuries, is an enormous thing — and Allah knows best. The meaning of "لَتَنُوءُ بِالعُصْبَةِ" is: would weigh down the band. Abū Zayd said: one says "نُؤْتُ بِالحِمْلِ، أنُوءُ بِهِ، نُوءًا" when I rise with the load, and "ناءَ بِيَ الحِمْلُ" when it weighs me down.
And His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ لا تَفْرَحْ إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الفَرِحِينَ﴾: it has come in the exegesis: do not be insolent; Allah does not love the insolent. "لا تَفْرَحْ" here — and Allah knows best — means: do not exult in the abundance of wealth in this world, because one who exults in wealth and spends it on other than the affair of the Hereafter is blameworthy in it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 23]. The evidence that they meant "do not exult in wealth in this world" is their saying: ﴿وابْتَغِ فِيما آتاكَ اللَّهُ الدّارَ الآخِرَةَ ولا تَنْسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ الدُّنْيا وأحْسِنْ كَما أحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إلَيْكَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 77]. "ولا تَنْسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ الدُّنْيا", i.e. "do not forget to work with it for your Hereafter", because the true share of a person from this world is that with which he works for his Hereafter.

zajjaj:78-78.t: ﴿قالَ إنَّما أُوتِيتُهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ عِنْدِي﴾: he claimed that he had been given the wealth because of his knowledge of the Torah. As for what is narrated, that he used to practise alchemy — this is not sound, because alchemy is false and has no reality.

zajjaj:79-79.t: And His saying: ﴿فَخَرَجَ عَلى قَوْمِهِ في زِينَتِهِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that he and his companions went out on their horses, with purple (al-urjuwān) on them and on the horses. "al-urjuwān (الأُرْجُوانُ)" in the language is a red dye. It was also said: they and their horses wore red brocade.

zajjaj:80-80.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلا يُلَقّاها إلا الصّابِرُونَ﴾, i.e. none is granted this deed and this word — meaning their saying: ﴿وَيْلَكم ثَوابُ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِمَن آمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا﴾ — [except the patient].

zajjaj:82-82.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَأصْبَحَ الَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوْا مَكانَهُ بِالأمْسِ﴾ means those who said: ﴿يا لَيْتَ لَنا مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيَ قارُونُ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 79]. ﴿يَقُولُونَ ويْكَأنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشاءُ مِن عِبادِهِ ويَقْدِرُ لَوْلا أنْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا لَخَسَفَ بِنا ويْكَأنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ﴾: this word, the word "وَيْكَ", has puzzled a number of the philologists. It has come in the exegesis that its meaning is: "Have you not seen that the disbelievers will not succeed? (ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ)"; and some of them said its meaning is: "Do you not see that the disbelievers will not succeed? (أما تَرى أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ)". One of the grammarians said — and this is a great error — that its meaning is: "Woe to you, know that the disbelievers will not succeed (وَيْلَكَ اعْلَمْ أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ)", and that the lām was dropped so that "وَيْكَ" remained, and "اِعْلَمْ" was dropped [before] "أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ". This is wrong from more than one angle. Had it been as he said, "أنَّ" would have had a kasra (إنَّ), as you say: "Woe to you, it has been such and such (وَيْلَكَ إنَّهُ قَدْ كانَ كَذا وكَذا)". From another angle: it would then be said to whoever addressed the people with this, and they said: "Woe to you, the disbelievers will not succeed." [Translator's note: the sentence is elliptical in the source; the point seems to be that on this view the expression would have to be addressed to a particular person.] From yet another angle: he dropped the lām from "وَيْلَ". The correct view on this is what Sībawayh mentioned from al-Khalīl and Yūnus. He said: I asked al-Khalīl about it, and he held that it is "وَيْ", separated from "كَأنَّ", and that the people became alert and said "وَيْ", regretting what had gone before from them. Everyone who regrets or repents shows his regret and remorse by saying "وَيْ", just as you reproach a man for what has gone before from him: saying "وَيْ" — as though you had aimed at what I dislike. So the proper pause on it is "وَيْ", and this is better in speech, and its meaning is alerting and regret. The poet said:
؎سَألَتانِي الطَّلاقَ إذْ رَأتانِي ∗∗∗ قَلَّ مالِي قَدْ جِئْتُما فِيَّ بِنُكْرِ
(The two of them asked me for divorce when they saw that my wealth had dwindled; you two have done me a monstrous thing.)
؎وَيْ كَأنْ مَن يَكُنْ لَهُ نَشَبٌ يُحْـ ∗∗∗ ـبَبْ ومَن يَفْتَقِرْ يَعِشْ عَيْشَ ضُرِّ؟!
(Ah! — it seems that whoever has property is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.)
This is al-Khalīl's explanation, and it agrees with what has come in the exegesis, because the exegetes' statement is: it is an alerting.

zajjaj:85-85.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِي فَرَضَ عَلَيْكَ القُرْآنَ لَرادُّكَ إلى مَعادٍ﴾: the meaning of "فَرَضَ عَلَيْكَ القُرْآنَ" is: He sent it down to you and made it binding on you, and made obligatory upon you acting on what the Qur'an requires.
﴿لَرادُّكَ إلى مَعادٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis: He will return you to your place in Mecca; and it was said: "إلى مَعادٍ" means to your place in Paradise. Most of the exegesis is: He will surely resurrect you; and on this is people's saying: "Remember the return (اُذْكُرِ المَعادَ)", i.e. remember your being raised in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:86-86.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلا تَكُونَنَّ ظَهِيرًا لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾, i.e. a helper to the disbelievers. "فَلا تَكُونَنْ ظَهِيرًا" (with the light nūn) is permissible, but I dislike it, because it differs from the Muṣḥaf: with the light form it would have to be written with an alif.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
And His saying: ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هالِكٌ إلا وجْهَهُ﴾: "وَجْهَهُ" is accusative by exception, and the meaning of "إلّا وجْهَهُ" is: except Him. "إلّا وجْهُهُ" in the nominative is permissible, but it ought not to be read; then the meaning is: "everything other than His Face is perishing (كُلُّ شَيْءٍ غَيْرُ وجْهِهِ هالِكٌ)". It is like the saying of the poet:
؎وَكُلُّ أخٍ مُفارِقُهُ أخُوهُ ∗∗∗ لَعَمْرَ أبِيكَ إلّا الفَرْقَدانِ
(Every brother is parted from by his brother — by your father's life — except the two Farqad stars.)
The meaning is: "every brother other than the two Farqad stars is parted from by his brother (وَكُلُّ أخٍ غَيْرُ الفَرْقَدَيْنِ مُفارِقُهُ أخُوهُ)".
